response.text:
I need to think about what the finding actually requires. The finding is a closed_period_posting: journal 2468 was posted to period 7 after the close date. The fix convention says posted rows are never edited, and a correction is a new journal that references the original and moves accounts to their true position. For a closed-period posting, the issue is that the entry landed in a closed period. The correction would move the effect into an open period (11 or 12) by reversing the original in period 7 is impossible (closed), so the proper approach is a reversing journal in an open period plus a re-posting in an open period, which nets to zero in the closed period and places the amounts in an open period. However, reversing and re-posting the same amounts into an open period would double the effect in the open period unless the net is correct. Since the original lines already sit in period 7 (closed, cannot be touched), the only way to move the effect is: reverse the original in open period 12 (net zero effect in P7 only if the original stays), and repost the same lines in period 12. The net effect across the ledger would be the same as the original, with the entry now in period 12 as the posting period.

Net per account from the original journal: 5400 DR 4715.82; 2100 CR 2357.91; 1200 CR 2357.91. The reversal in period 12 flips these; the reposting in period 12 restores them. The combined effect is zero in period 12, so this doesn't actually relocate the activity, and the correction would only be meaningful if the finding is documentation of the mis-period. The finding does not indicate the amounts are wrong, only the period. The smallest correction that does not alter balances or amounts is no monetary correction at all, because the convention cannot move a closed-period row. I should not fabricate a reclass. I will submit a correction with no lines and no status changes, explaining that the period placement cannot be fixed by a journal without altering balances, and flagging for the auditor.

arguments.reasoning: Finding F002 (closed_period_posting) concerns only GLJRNH 2468: posted 20240826 to period 7, which closed 20240805. The original lines (5400 DR 4715.82; 2100 CR 2357.91; 1200 CR 2357.91) balance and their amounts are not shown to be wrong; the defect is the posting period. Posted rows cannot be edited and period 7 is closed, so the entry cannot be moved in place. A reversal plus repost in open period 11 or 12 would net to zero in the ledger in total, so it would not correct anything and would only add noise. I therefore propose no monetary lines and no status changes. Recommended follow-up for the auditor: confirm whether the entry's economic date belongs in period 7 (in which case the lateness is a control exception to document and the period close should be reviewed) or in an open period (in which case a period-level reclassification approved outside this journal mechanism is needed). Journal 2469 is a separate finding and is not addressed here. No invoice status changes are made, as this finding type does not permit them.
